strengths: Novel first-of-its-kind identification of pruning as an attack trigger with significant practical implications for deployed systems like vLLM
Realistic threat model reflecting actual deployment scenarios where users download and prune models without adversary involvement post-release
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 5 models, 3 pruning algorithms, multiple pruning configurations, and 3 diverse attack scenarios with consistently high success rates
Strong technical insight that pruning scores correlate between methods, enabling effective targeting via single-metric (Wanda) pre-estimation with >99% accuracy
Thorough analysis including ablations, cross-dataset robustness, and honest assessment of defense limitations in §6.3
Demonstrated genuine stealthiness with utility preservation before pruning (Table 1) and comparable benchmarks to base models
Clear presentation with well-motivated figures, detailed pseudocode, and comprehensive appendices supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Incomplete defense solutions: security-aware calibration has utility costs and limited effect on Wanda; optimal patching requires oracle knowledge; practical defenses remain elusive

Limited scope restricted to unstructured pruning in vLLM; structured pruning, LoRA-based methods, and other compression techniques not explored; generalization to 70B+ models and diverse architectures unclear

Evaluation concerns including high base model jailbreak ASR in some models (Mistral 43.7%) making attack attribution ambiguous, reliance on single LLM judge (GPT-4.1-mini) without cross-validation, and severe performance degradation in some 2:4 pruning scenarios reducing realism

Incomplete practical context: unclear which model provider scenarios are most at risk, realistic timeline of adversary pre-release model possession not discussed, and comparison with exploitation difficulty of other post-training attacks missing
Attack generalization limitations including dependence on known pruning procedures and calibration dataset similarity; robustness demonstrated but not exhaustively characterized
Technical design choices with limited justification: αinj=50% and scenario-specific αrep values (1-5%) appear empirically tuned; missing ablation on αinj in §6.1
Code availability promised but not provided in submission; responsible disclosure timeline not mentioned
